newsitem.title: USA: EEOC in pact with Texaco on race case.
newsitem.headline: EEOC in pact with Texaco on race case.

text.p: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission told a federal judge Friday that it had reached an agreement with Texaco Inc that would allow the EEOC to intervene in a racial discrimination case pending against the company.
U.S. District Judge Charles Brieant then issued a scheduling order setting a hearing on February 27 1997 to consider approving the settlement.
The agreement between Texaco and the EEOC relates to a 1994 discrimination lawsuit that was filed against Texaco alleging that it had discriminated in pay and promotions against black employees.
In November the plaintiffs reached a tentative settlement with Texaco in which the company agreed to pay $176.1 million and agreed to establish an "equality and tolerance" task force.
The EEOC was troubled that it had been excluded from the settlement talks and has been negotiating with Texaco to obtain a monitoring role in the settlement.

Under the agreement reached between Texaco and the EEOC, the EEOC can monitor Texaco's compliance with federal law by inspecting Texaco's premises and records as well as interviewing current or former employees.
Other provisions include Texaco's agreement to give the EEOC a written plan for examining the potential adverse impact on minorities for its plan for future promotions.

At the end of one year from the effective date of the agreement and every year for the next five years, Texaco must give a report to the EEOC about vacancies filled by promotion to ensure that Afro-Americans and other minorities are promoted in compliance with the agreements reached and federal laws.

Also during Friday's hearing, Daniel Berger, an attorney for the African-American plaintiffs, told the judge that he will submit by January 10 1997 the formal settlement agreement reached between the plaintiffs and Texaco.

He said that notice will be sent to all possible members of the class action by January 17 1997. Those employees who want to object to the settlement or opt out of the agreement must file their objections with the court by February 20 1997.
